skill.name: backend-architect
skill.description: Guides backend architecture work with hexagonal architecture, DDD, SOLID, clean code, refactoring, testing, and code review practices.
skill.summary: Backend architecture assistant for design, review, refactoring, and quality checks.
skill.author: Bikach

security_audit.summary: The static weak-crypto and reconnaissance alerts are false positives from French prose, Markdown filenames, test names, and architecture terms. The shell-backtick alerts are Markdown inline code references to directories or normal review commands, not executable shell code. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious workflow was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: Broad Bash tool access for a documentation-oriented architecture skill.
remediation.suggestion: If supported, narrow command use to read-only review commands and require user approval for linters, formatters, or project scripts.

content.value_statement: Backend teams need consistent guidance for architecture, reviews, tests, and refactoring. This skill provides structured backend design checks using hexagonal architecture, DDD, SOLID, and clean code practices.
actual_capabilities: Reviews backend changes for architecture, SOLID, code smells, test coverage, and performance concerns.
Suggests bounded contexts, ports, adapters, repositories, gateways, and dependency injection boundaries.
Provides prioritized feedback with location, impact, recommendation, and examples when useful.
Guides refactoring for God Class, Feature Envy, Primitive Obsession, Long Method, and related smells.
Uses included checklists and examples to compare proposed backend designs against documented patterns.
limitations: Does not execute migrations, deployments, or production changes by itself.
Requires access to relevant project files or diffs for accurate review.
Provides architectural guidance, but teams must validate decisions against business requirements.
May need project-specific conventions to avoid generic recommendations.

use_cases.title: Review a feature branch
use_cases.description: Assess recent backend changes for layering, dependencies, code smells, and tests before merging.

use_cases.title: Plan a new service boundary
use_cases.description: Define bounded contexts, ports, adapters, and integration points for a new backend feature.

use_cases.title: Guide targeted refactoring
use_cases.description: Identify high-impact refactoring steps for complex services without rewriting unrelated code.

prompt_templates.title: Review a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this backend diff for architecture, clean code, tests, and obvious risks. Prioritize the top issues and suggest direct fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a feature structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Help design a backend feature using hexagonal architecture. Identify domain objects, use cases, ports, adapters, and test boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a complex service
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this service for SOLID violations and code smells. Propose an incremental refactoring plan with risks, order, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an architecture decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this backend architecture decision against DDD, dependency inversion, performance, testing, and maintainability. Challenge weak assumptions and propose alternatives.

output_examples.input: Review a new account registration flow.
output: Findings are grouped by priority with file locations and impact.
The response separates domain validation, persistence, and notification concerns.
It recommends focused tests for domain rules and adapter behavior.

output_examples.input: Plan a module for invoice exports.
output: The answer proposes domain objects, application use cases, ports, adapters, and test boundaries.
It calls out infrastructure leakage risks before implementation starts.
It gives verification steps for export rules and adapter integration.
The response identifies separate responsibilities and risky dependencies.
It proposes incremental extraction steps instead of a large rewrite.
It includes test checkpoints before changing persistence or external adapters.

best_practices: Share the relevant diff, architecture context, and existing conventions before asking for a review.
Ask for prioritized findings when you need merge-ready feedback.
Use its recommendations as design input, then validate with tests and team review.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to rewrite an entire codebase without clear boundaries.
Do not treat generic architecture advice as a replacement for domain knowledge.
Do not skip tests because the suggested design looks clean.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with backend design, reviews, refactoring, code smells, SOLID checks, and test strategy.

faq.question: Which architecture style does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes hexagonal architecture, DDD boundaries, dependency inversion, and clean separation between domain and infrastructure.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide files or diffs so it can locate issues and suggest focused changes.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: The source mentions git diff, grep, linters, and formatters as review tools. Users should approve command use in their environment.

faq.question: Is it only for TypeScript?
faq.answer: No. The guidance is language-neutral, but examples focus on common backend architecture patterns.

faq.question: How should teams use the output?
faq.answer: Treat output as review guidance. Confirm recommendations with tests, standards, and domain experts.
